review.regression_record: Six evaluations were added on 2026-08-04 after live device validation on a Zebra TC701 / Android 15 / DataWedge 15.0.73 found five real defects in previously inspection-only content: adf-device-verified-write-shape, adf-antipattern-rule-order-shadowing, adf-antipattern-ownership-crash, adf-antipattern-result-info-success, adf-antipattern-unbounded-readback, and adf-positional-reorder-outcome. Each encodes a failure observed on hardware. Ordering disclosure: the defects were found and corrected during live debugging, so these evaluations were written immediately after each fix rather than as failing-first tests. Each one was, however, demonstrably failing on the pre-fix build - the observed failure evidence is recorded in every case. The user approved this backport explicitly; the skill remains an unreleased draft at 1.0.0-beta.1, so no version increment is owed.
review.review_detail_record: Evaluations 1-4 (adf-route-intent-output, adf-route-handoff-profile-setup, adf-rule-replace-string-bundle, adf-criteria-decoder-scoped-rule) were presented individually with full prompt, expected output, assertions, and files, and approved one at a time. At evaluation 4 the user selected bulk approval for all remaining evaluations as scoped in the portfolio overview (ID, category, purpose). Evaluations 5-15 therefore carry explicit user approval at overview level, not assertion-level review. Assertion-level review of evaluations 5-15 is disclosed as remaining work.
review.execution_note: No evaluation in this portfolio has been executed as a scripted test; they are authored acceptance criteria, not harness results. However, the six regression evaluations added on 2026-08-04 encode behaviour actually observed on a Zebra TC701 / Android 15 / DataWedge 15.0.73: each failure they guard was reproduced on hardware, and each fix was confirmed on hardware. Achieved validation level for the skill is therefore 'device' for the ADF write shape, rule ordering, success detection, readback parsing, and the end-to-end transformation, and 'inspection' for everything else. See references/sources.md.

coverage_not_applicable.manual-fallback: This skill ships no scripts and makes no live checks, so no script fallback route exists to evaluate. The text-first manual procedure is covered by adf-offline-no-shell.
coverage_not_applicable.starter-validation: No assets/starters/ is bundled. A runnable starter was deliberately excluded because no Android SDK or Gradle toolchain was available to clean-build it, and an unverified runnable claim is not permitted.

evals.purpose: REGRESSION for AP-11. Observed on device: a scoped rule merged behind the auto-created Rule0 never fires, while SET_CONFIG reports SUCCESS and a readback confirms the rule exists. Rule present and verified is not rule effective.
evals.prompt: I added a rule scoped to string_len 13 using RESET_CONFIG false so I would not lose anything. SET_CONFIG returned SUCCESS and a readback shows my rule is there, but scans still arrive completely unchanged. Why?
evals.expected_output: Identifies rule shadowing: evaluation is ordered, the first matching rule wins, and the auto-created Rule0 has no criteria so it matches everything and sits first. Merging appends rather than reorders, so specificity confers no priority. Prescribes RESET_CONFIG=true with PARAM_LIST carrying every rule in order, most specific first and catch-all last, re-supplying a passthrough because clearing Rule0 leaves non-matching input with no rule, then confirming order by readback.
assertions: Identifies rule ordering / shadowing as the cause, not a malformed rule.
States that the first matching rule wins and that Rule0 has no criteria.
States that merging cannot reposition a rule.
Prescribes RESET_CONFIG=true plus re-supplying all rules in order.
Requires the catch-all passthrough to be LAST.
Warns that clearing Rule0 leaves non-matching input with no rule unless a passthrough is re-supplied.
Notes that a readback confirming existence does not prove effectiveness.
Requires confirming the resulting order by readback.

evals.purpose: REGRESSION for AP-12. The single-owner guard threw IllegalStateException from the constructor and crashed the app on ordinary activity recreation - the enforcement was worse than the bug it prevented.
evals.prompt: Review this ownership guard: a process-wide set of claimed profile names, check(set.add(profileName)) throwing from the configurator constructor, and the claim released only when the host isFinishing.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the design. Android constructs a recreated Activity before destroying the old one, so an overlapping claim is normal and transient, and releasing only on isFinishing guarantees a collision on rotation or configuration change. Prescribes a per-profile registry whose factory returns the existing instance instead of throwing, with a settable stateListener the host clears on destroy so a process-scoped owner never retains a destroyed Activity. Notes that recreation then reattaches to the same owner and keeps its readiness state.
assertions: Identifies that throwing from the constructor makes a normal lifecycle event fatal.
States that Android creates the new instance before destroying the old one.
Identifies releasing only on isFinishing as insufficient.
Prescribes a per-profile registry / factory that returns the existing instance.
Requires a clearable state listener so a destroyed Activity is not retained.
Notes that the single-owner invariant itself is correct and must be preserved, not dropped.
Does not propose downgrading the guard to a silent no-op that permits two competing owners.

evals.purpose: REGRESSION for AP-13. Requiring an empty RESULT_INFO made every success read as a failure and retried into a blocked state, because DataWedge returns {PROFILE_NAME=...} alongside RESULT=SUCCESS.
evals.prompt: My success check is: result == "SUCCESS" && resultInfo.isEmpty(). Every SET_CONFIG logs RESULT=SUCCESS but my app reports it failed after three attempts. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the RESULT_INFO condition as the defect: RESULT carries the outcome, RESULT_INFO carries detail and is not empty on success - DataWedge 15.0.73 returns {PROFILE_NAME=<profile>}. Prescribes testing RESULT == SUCCESS alone and checking RESULT_INFO values against the terminal result codes. Additionally notes that SUCCESS proves acceptance, not rule creation, and only a readback proves creation.
assertions: Identifies the isEmpty() condition on RESULT_INFO as the defect.
States that RESULT_INFO carries {PROFILE_NAME=...} on success.
Prescribes testing RESULT == SUCCESS alone.
Retains inspection of RESULT_INFO values against terminal result codes.
Notes that SUCCESS means accepted, not created, and only a readback proves creation.
Attributes the behaviour to device evidence on DataWedge 15.0.73.

evals.purpose: REGRESSION for AP-14. The verification path had no attempt cap, so an unrecognised readback shape produced a broadcast storm - 12+ GET_CONFIG sends in under 5 seconds with no convergence and no error surfaced.
evals.prompt: My write path retries at most 3 times, then I loop requesting GET_CONFIG until the readback confirms the rule, since readbacks are cheap and idempotent. Any problem?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the verification loop as unbounded. The write succeeded so the write-path cap never engages, and any unrecognised readback shape - including the documented-versus-actual PARAM_LIST mismatch - loops forever, flooding DataWedge and surfacing no error. Prescribes a separate bounded counter on the verification path that fails into an explicit blocked reason, and reporting could-not-confirm as a real outcome the host must see.
assertions: Identifies the verification loop as unbounded and distinct from the write-path cap.
Explains that a successful write means the write cap never engages.
Names an unrecognised readback shape as a realistic trigger.
Prescribes a separate bounded counter for the verification path.
Requires failing into an explicit blocked reason rather than retrying forever.
States that could-not-confirm is a reportable outcome, not a reason to keep retrying.

evals.purpose: Device-verified end-to-end outcome, and the canonical demonstration that ADF has no reverse action - reversal must be unrolled, so the action count scales with a fixed known length.
evals.prompt: Deliver only the 3rd digit, then the 1st digit, then digits 4 to 13 in reverse, for 13-digit barcodes. All transformation must happen in DataWedge; my app must not touch the string.
evals.expected_output: States that ADF has no reverse action, no loop, and no length arithmetic, so reversal is unrolled one character at a time and the fixed length is mandatory. Produces output positions [3,1,13,12,11,10,9,8,7,6,5,4] as 35 actions using SKIP_TO_START plus SKIP_AHEAD n-1 plus SEND_NEXT 1 per character, with no terminal SEND_REMAINING because truncation is intended. Notes that absolute positioning avoids depending on whether SEND_NEXT advances the cursor. Gives 8055002861991 to 581991682005 as the device-confirmed result, and requires the catch-all passthrough last with RESET_CONFIG true.

Confirms the app performs no string manipulation on the payload.

evals.purpose: Protects AP-1. RESET_CONFIG defaults to true, which clears existing configuration and silently destroys sibling ADF rules while still reporting success.
evals.prompt: My push worked but two ADF rules that another team created are now gone. Here is what I sent: PLUGIN_NAME ADF, OUTPUT_PLUGIN_NAME INTENT, RESET_CONFIG true, CONFIG_MODE OVERWRITE. What happened and how do I stop it?

Explains that SET_CONFIG still reports success, so the loss is silent. Prescribes RESET_CONFIG=false with CONFIG_MODE=UPDATE, and a readback before pushing so existing rules are known first. Warns against re-pushing rules whose full content is unknown.

evals.purpose: Protects AP-2 and AP-3. Two owners of profile/ADF state plus duplicate RESULT_ACTION registration produce interleaved config, doubled handling, and stale-result consumption, made worse because DataWedge does not queue commands.
evals.prompt: My Activity configures ADF in onResume and a foreground Service also pushes ADF config at startup. Each registers its own receiver for com.symbol.datawedge.api.RESULT_ACTION. Sometimes the rule is right, sometimes it is the old one, and it changes between runs. Review this design.
evals.expected_output: Names competing ownership and duplicate receiver registration as the defects. Explains that DataWedge does not queue API commands so one push may be dropped, making the surviving configuration nondeterministic, and that with COMMAND_IDENTIFIER unchecked one component consumes the other's result and reports success for a command it never sent. Prescribes exactly one AdfIntentOutputConfigurator per profile enforced by the LIVE_OWNERS check, one registration per process routed through DwResultRouter, and COMMAND_IDENTIFIER matching that drops non-matching, duplicate, and late results.
assertions: Identifies competing ownership of ADF state as a defect.
Identifies duplicate RESULT_ACTION registration as a defect.
Explains nondeterminism via DataWedge not queueing API commands.
Explains that an unmatched COMMAND_IDENTIFIER lets one component consume another's result.
Prescribes exactly one configurator per profile and one receiver registration per process.
Names the LIVE_OWNERS check and DwResultRouter as the enforcing mechanisms.
Requires dropping non-matching, duplicate, and late results.

evals.purpose: Proves every declared callback maps to an exact host action and an exact local code location, with lifecycle, threading, idempotency, failure, and teardown behavior stated. A callback name or comment alone is incomplete wiring.
evals.prompt: Show me exactly what my app must do for every DataWedge callback in this pattern - which function, at which lifecycle point, on which thread, what happens on duplicate or late delivery, and what to tear down.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces the callback-to-host-action map: onHostStart registers then reconciles; onDataWedgeResult matches COMMAND_IDENTIFIER, reads RESULT and RESULT_INFO, then reconciles; readbackMatchesRequestedRule sets verifiedByReadback; timeoutRunnable retries; terminal codes set blockedReason and stop; onStateChanged is the host UI action; ScanDataReceiver.onReceive consumes data_string; onHostStop unregisters, cancels the timeout and drops the token; release frees the owner claim. States that onReceive runs on the main thread and must not block, that duplicate and late results are dropped by token mismatch, and that teardown is symmetric with registration and never disables the profile.
assertions: Every callback is mapped to a named function, not to a comment or interface name.
Lifecycle points are stated for registration and teardown.
States that BroadcastReceiver.onReceive runs on the main thread and must not block.
Duplicate and late result handling is specified as dropped via COMMAND_IDENTIFIER mismatch.
Terminal result codes are shown setting blockedReason and stopping retries.

evals.purpose: Protects AP-4. Receiver registration (R2) and ADF application (R4) complete independently, so both completion orders, cold and warm start, duplicate and late signals, cancellation and shutdown must all converge through one idempotent reconciliation path.
evals.prompt: Walk every completion order for this integration: the SET_CONFIG result arriving before my receiver is registered, the receiver being ready long before DataWedge answers, a warm restart where the rule is already applied, two results for one command, a result arriving after onStop, and a command superseded mid-flight. What must happen in each case?
evals.expected_output: Covers all six orders. Result-before-registration is rescued by the timeout routing into reconcileAdfState rather than being lost. Receiver-ready-first waits and reconciles on result arrival. Warm restart with the rule already applied is confirmed by readback and issues no redundant SET_CONFIG. A duplicate result is a no-op with no second readback. A late result after onStop is dropped with no crash and no state mutation. A superseded command has its token rotated so only the newest settles state. States that all four edges - onHostStart, result, readback, timeout - call the same re-entrancy-guarded reconcileAdfState, and that retrying from only one edge is a one-sided retry causing a missed wakeup.
assertions: All six completion orders are addressed explicitly.
Result-before-registration is recovered via the timeout path, not left hanging.
Warm restart with the rule already applied issues no redundant SET_CONFIG.
Duplicate results are a no-op and trigger no second readback.
Late results after teardown are dropped without crashing or mutating state.
Superseded commands are handled by rotating COMMAND_IDENTIFIER.
Names all four reconciliation trigger edges calling one idempotent function.
Explicitly identifies one-sided retry as the missed-wakeup defect.

evals.purpose: Protects AP-5 and AP-6. A cached configured flag and a bare success result are both weaker than the freshness contract, which only a GET_CONFIG plus PROCESS_PLUGIN_NAME readback satisfies.
evals.prompt: To save startup time I store adfConfigured=true in SharedPreferences after the first successful SET_CONFIG and skip configuration on later launches. My SET_CONFIG returned success, so the rule is definitely there, right?
evals.expected_output: Rejects both assumptions. A cached flag does not satisfy freshness because DataWedge configuration can change through a DataWedge upgrade or data clear, a user edit, an MX configuration, or another app taking the profile. A success result is not proof the rule is stored. Prescribes GET_CONFIG with PROCESS_PLUGIN_NAME as the only fresh confirmation, notes that a plain GET_CONFIG cannot read process plug-ins so an empty ADF section means wrong query rather than no rule, and states that verifiedByReadback is per-session and never persisted.

Requires GET_CONFIG with PROCESS_PLUGIN_NAME as the fresh confirmation.
